page: Amazon Web Services c8i.metal-96xl is a bare-metal compute-optimized server powered by dual-socket Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 192 physical cores and 384 vCPUs running at up to 3.9 GHz, backed by 480 MB of shared L3 cache and dedicated hardware execution with no hypervisor layer. System memory totals 768.0 GB of high-frequency DDR5 RAM at 7 GHz, providing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Networking features a dedicated 100 Gbps baseline interface. The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage or discrete GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage architectures.

Benchmark measurements confirm massive multi-core compute capability. In stress-ng testing, multi-core throughput scored in the top tier at 417,805.84, while single-core performance remained in the median range at 2,140.9. Extended instruction support via AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8 drives top-tier PassMark CPU extended instruction (476,593.49) and CPU encryption (422,513.19) metrics. High-throughput tasks like Clang compilation, ray tracing, and multi-threaded decompression all rank in the top 10% bracket. Similarly, read-only memory bandwidth delivers 1,170.89 GB/sec uncached, enabling 510.74 million Redis SET operations per second and high static web serving throughput.

The hardware configuration offers exceptional density for parallelized execution where compute scales linearly with core counts. Because memory is constrained to 2.0 GB per vCPU and local disk storage is absent, workloads requiring expansive memory-to-core footprints or low-latency direct-attached disks face clear architectural tradeoffs. Sequential text generation on language models without GPU acceleration also exhibits modest performance despite strong matrix prompt processing speeds.

The c8i.metal-96xl server is optimized for high-performance computing (HPC), continuous integration build farms, distributed microservice virtualization, video transcoding, CPU-based matrix processing, and intensive in-memory caching tiers.
